title: Transcriptome-based machine learning reveals an MCL1 dependency in alveolar soft part sarcoma
summary: A support-vector-regression model trained to infer gene dependencies from RNA-sequencing profiles predicted selective MCL1 dependence in alveolar soft part sarcoma (ASPS), distinct from TFE3-translocation renal cell carcinoma. The authors tested the prediction with CRISPR knockout and the MCL1 inhibitor murizatoclax in two ASPS cell lines; the reported viability effects were greater in ASPS than comparator tRCC lines.
ai_technology: Transcriptome-based support-vector regression model (RBF kernel; 657 highly predictable gene dependencies)
organization: Dana-Farber Cancer Institute; Broad Institute of MIT and Harvard

evidence.tested: The authors tested the prediction with CRISPR knockout and the MCL1 inhibitor murizatoclax in two ASPS cell lines; the reported viability effects were greater in ASPS than comparator tRCC lines.
evidence.unknown: bioRxiv preprint, not peer reviewed as stated by PMC. Validation was in two ASPS cell lines with CRISPR and inhibitor assays; it does not establish patient benefit or clinical efficacy. The model nominates dependencies and is not a functional screen itself.
evidence.ai_role: The model predicted per-gene dependency scores from tumor/cell-line expression profiles and prioritized selective vulnerabilities. The study then tested MCL1 dependence in ASPS using three distinct sgRNAs and murizatoclax; those experiments, rather than the prediction alone, provide the reported validation.
